mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) from the prior month signals an easing monetary policy stance, which reduces discount rates for equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declined from the prior month, or the rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth exceeds 146,000 jobs per month, it signals a tight labor market that accelerates consumer spending and corporate profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS > 146000, or the rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) from the prior month indicates robust aggregate demand that elevates corporate revenue expectations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS and HOUST both increased from the prior month, or the rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO < 104.0) combined with moderate GDP growth (GDPC1 > 16800) indicates an early economic deceleration phase that reduces corporate profit growth expectations, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 104.0 and GDPC1 > 16800, or the rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.
